title: Brainstem regions: native MRI, probabilities and independent masks
author: NeuroImage project
objective: Relate twelve source-defined brainstem regions to their supplied MRI context; distinguish full population support, independent binary memberships and navigation surfaces.

scenes.title: Paired red nuclei with nigral context
scenes.prompt: Start with the complete source MRI sections to establish global location. Use Magnify at cursor to inspect the selected left red nucleus, then Full sections to recover the surrounding context. Compare its position with the paired nucleus and the translucent nigral masks.
scenes.note: The colored probability field belongs only to the selected region. Each 3D surface follows its own delivered binary mask. The source cohort comprises twelve healthy adults; population overlap is not individual tissue certainty.

scenes.title: Binary navigation boundary in FA context
scenes.prompt: Compare this binary mask with the preceding probability view at the same source target. Observe the supplied FA contrast without treating it as a tractography map.
scenes.note: The source mask retains probabilities greater than or equal to 0.35. The full probability field remains available. Diffusion fractional anisotropy is a scalar MRI measure, not a displayed fiber pathway.

scenes.title: Superior and inferior collicular source regions
scenes.prompt: Locate the selected inferior colliculus and compare its position with the source superior collicular masks. Follow adjacent sections before interpreting the apparent separation.
scenes.note: These are source-defined population regions at 1 mm sampling. The surfaces do not establish a complete histological border, a neural connection or an individual functional map.

scenes.title: Two independent memberships at one source voxel
scenes.prompt: Read the two source-mask memberships at the cursor. Select Dorsal raphe in the membership list to change the probability field while retaining this physical location. Return to the recorded view before continuing.
scenes.note: The recorded voxel belongs to both delivered PAG and DR binary masks. Both memberships are retained. Overlap of population atlas regions is not proof of tissue interpenetration in an individual.

scenes.title: Positive source support outside the binary boundary
scenes.prompt: Read the selected PAG probability of 0.15 at this source voxel. Switch to the binary-mask overlay to observe that this voxel is outside the delivered 0.35 navigation mask.
scenes.note: This sample demonstrates why a thresholded surface does not contain every positive source probability. Neither the binary boundary nor low population support alone establishes an individual tissue boundary.

scenes.title: Paired inferior olivary source regions
scenes.prompt: Follow the selected inferior olivary mask in axial, coronal and sagittal MRI. Rotate the paired source surfaces around the recorded point and compare both sides.
scenes.note: The BIlab templates have partial brain coverage. Sampling, source delineation and population averaging limit the interpretation of small contours. No smoothing or new anatomical detail has been added.
